author: mayhem82
reason: First real evidence-collection run for DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 (RUN-0001, per spec section 6's permitted automation sequence), following the operator's instruction to begin substantive investigation. Added 8 evidence items, 13 sources (5 web-search queries, per section 27), 6 chronology entries, and 5 open questions, all grounded in preserved and hashed primary/secondary sources. Updated case.json's current_status and repository_version (now legitimately mutable tracking fields per the updated Mutable vs. Append-Only Fields section in docs/DATA_MODEL.md).

author: mayhem82
reason: Added a live Investigation Notes register and workspace view (spec section 14) - an append-only working log written progressively during a collection run, rendered most-recent-first and polled every 15s in the browser so it reflects work in progress rather than only a static end-of-session summary. Used it to log RUN-0002, a follow-up evidence-collection run pursuing RUN-0001's unpursued leads: added EV-0009 (pushes the known drought onset back to June 2019) and EV-0010 (first Bellbrook-specific evidence since 2020, partially informing but not resolving Q-0002). Recorded DEC-0006, a standing rule against working around bot-detection blocks after a Wayback Machine snapshot of a blocked source could not be retrieved.

author: mayhem82
reason: RUN-0003, continuing evidence collection at the operator's request while they separately attempt the four blocked kempsey.nsw.gov.au URLs with their own browser tools. Added EV-0011/EV-0012 (resolving Q-0004, the mayoral transition) and EV-0013 (pushes the Willawarrin plant's documented history back to May 2022). Closed THR-15 and Q-0004; opened Q-0006 for a residual date discrepancy in EV-0011 that could not be independently confirmed either way. Ruled out the WaterNSW 2025 compliance report as inapplicable (logged as a note, not a source, since it was checked and found not to mention this case at all).

author: mayhem82
reason: Made the workspace a real, navigable website per the operator's request. (1) Added a GitHub Actions workflow publishing the repository root to GitHub Pages on every push to main. Moved the workspace (index.html, app.js, style.css) from site/ to the repository root, updating its data/ fetch paths accordingly, so the workspace itself is the site's main page - not something behind a /site/ subpath or a redirect stub - per follow-up operator feedback that the initial redirect-based approach wasn't the intended design. (2) Every cross-reference ID a register cites (relationships, supporting_evidence, dependencies, etc., previously rendered as inert text chips) is now a real link: clicking it switches to the owning section, opens and scrolls to that specific record, and updates the URL to a shareable #section/RECORD-ID deep link; section and record navigation now use history.pushState on user clicks (previously always replaceState) so browser back/forward works like ordinary page navigation.

author: mayhem82
reason: RUN-0004: reconciles a separate, unmerged evidence-collection branch (also self-identified as 'RUN-0003') that duplicated this repository's already-committed CHG-0007 mayoral-transition evidence with a weaker, search-snippet-only version of the same facts. That duplicate (its own EV-0011, a chronology entry, and a THR-15 update) was dropped as redundant/inferior rather than merged. Carried forward only what remained genuinely new from that branch's session: SRC-0023 (Council Public Forum, 20 July 2026 - confirmed to exist, blocked to fetch) and SRC-0024 (Steuart McIntyre Dam tender listing - confirms a tender ran, contractor still unnamed), plus DEC-0007 declining to accept an unverified 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' claim as evidence. Note: change_id CHG-0008 is reserved by a separate, still-open pull request (workspace navigation/GitHub Pages) opened before this one; skipping it here avoids a collision once both merge.

author: mayhem82
reason: RUN-0011, continuing evidence collection at the operator's request. Used pure calendar computation (no external fetch required) plus a statutory citation (SRC-0031, fetch-blocked) to build the strongest available non-primary-source case for Q-0006: 9 September 2024 was a Monday, while 14 September 2024 was specifically the second Saturday of that September, matching the Local Government Act's 'second Saturday in September' requirement exactly. Q-0006 strengthened but not closed - still requires a preserved primary citation.
